subject: Re: Renewal + competitive bakeoff — baseline metrics & proposal
thread_body:
From: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@zencommerce.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@zencommerce.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal / Bakeoff heads-up

Hi Logan,

Quick heads-up: our renewal for Redwood is up on Sep 15 and the execs have asked us to run a short vendor bakeoff — LumenAI is pushing hard on price and claims better latency at 2k token windows.

Before we commit time, can you: 1) share any recent benchmark artifacts for our typical workload (mid-size prompts, multi-turn chat, average sequence 800 tokens), 2) confirm how Redwood would support a side-by-side bakeoff (env, SLAs, data handling), and 3) outline any commercial guardrails / incentives you can put on the table if the bakeoff shows parity?

We value reliability and the operational controls you give us, but procurement wants concrete numbers to compare. Priya is coordinating the vendor tests on our side.

Thanks — Ethan
Principal Product Manager
ZenCommerce

---
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@zencommerce.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@zencommerce.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal / Bakeoff heads-up

Hi Ethan — thanks for the ping and for flagging the timeline. We99d like to make the bakeoff low-friction and bias it toward the signals you care about (p50/p95 token latency, throughput at 200 concurrent connections, consistency/hallucination rate on your eval set).

I've attached a lightweight bakeoff worksheet (zen_bakeoff_worksheet.xlsx) that captures the test harness we propose:
- workload spec: sample prompts + tokenization details
- two-run plan: baseline (current prod) + candidate (LumenAI)
- metric collection: latency distribution, tokens/sec, failure/retry rate, hallucination checks (your eval prompts)
- data handling: we can run in a sandboxed dedicated pool and provide signed NDA + isolated logs; we do not persist your raw prompts beyond the test window unless you instruct us to.

Commercially, our standard renewal posture is: 12-month renewal at current list with options to add committed capacity to lower unit price. Given a bakeoff, I can put forward:
- a conditional uplift offer: +15% committed tokens (12mo) with a stepped discount schedule (8% on committed usage) if benchmarks show parity on p95 latency and parity on hallucination rate;
- dedicated burst pool for peak-day throughput during the bakeoff;
- an SLA credit clause for the first 3 months post-renewal if latency exceeds agreed p95 targets.

If that aligns, I99ll schedule a kickoff next week and loop in our infra folks for the test harness. What date works for your team for the first run?

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0132

Attachment: zen_bakeoff_worksheet.xlsx (type: spreadsheet)

---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: internal: ZenCommerce save plan recommendation

Logan / Rishi,

Context: ZenCommerce is price-pressured and has an upcoming exec review. They care about p95 latency at 2k windows and deterministic burst capacity. LumenAI is offering an attractive headline price.

Recommendation:
- Offer the conditional uplift Logan outlined but sweeten the initial term with a 60-day "benchmark escrow": if Zen runs our bakeoff and finds parity on p95 and hallucination <= current, we convert to the committed uplift pricing automatically; otherwise revert to a full-month opt-out window.
- Add a one-time migration credit (9K USD) they can apply toward professional services for model tuning / quantization profile alignment.
- Commit to a bakeoff runbook with our infra SRE on-call and a 48-hour live troubleshooting window.

These give Zen visible upside if Redwood wins, and a clean escape if they prefer the other vendor. Approve to present to Ethan?

-M
Marissa Cole
Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

---
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: ZenCommerce save plan recommendation

+1 to Marissa's approach. A couple tactical notes:
- Keep the committed uplift band exclusive to instances where we can validate p95 on their eval set; we don't want open-ended credits if they test only microbenchmarks.
- Offer a short-term feature: enable KV cache snapshot sharing for the bakeoff so the candidate can be more realistic; this reduces false negatives for us.
- If procurement asks for extended payment terms in exchange for the uplift, push for a 12mo net-45 rather than 90.

Rishi
Head of Sales Ops

---
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@zencommerce.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@zencommerce.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal / Bakeoff heads-up — proposed schedule & conditional offer

Ethan / Priya,

Following internal alignment, here99s a concrete proposal and schedule we99re ready to commit to:

1) Bakeoff logistics
- Kickoff: Wed Jul 11, 09:00 PT (30m) to align instrumentation and test harness.
- Run window: Jul 12-15 (two full-run windows: baseline + candidate).
- Metrics we will publish: p50/95 latency (1k / 2k token windows), tokens/sec, tail error rate, hallucination rate on your eval set.
- Sandbox: dedicated pool isolated by tenant for the duration; logs exported to your S3 bucket (short-term access) and scrubbed after 30 days unless you request retention.

2) Commercial conditional offer (if bakeoff demonstrates parity on p95 and hallucination):
- 12-month renewal term starting Sep 15, 2028.
- +15% committed tokens on top of current baseline; committed usage qualifies for 8% discount on committed volume.
- One-time migration credit: $9,000 for tuning / quantization profiling.
- SLA credit: for first 90 days post-renewal, 5% monthly credit if p95 exceeds agreed threshold more than 3 times.
- DocuSign link for proposed term sheet (attached): redwood-term-sheet-v3.docx / https://www.docusign.net/DocuSign/envelope/ABC123456789

3) Contingency / escape
- If bakeoff fails to meet parity, Zen has a 30-day opt-out window following the test results and we revert to month-to-month until you decide.

If that looks reasonable I99ll book the kickoff and loop our infra SRE (will share contact). We99re prepared to run the benchmark with your eval prompts and can provide a short anonymized report (zen_benchmark-2028q2.pdf) after the runs.

Thanks and let me know preferred kickoff time if the Wed slot is bad.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0132

Attachment stubs: redwood-term-sheet-v3.docx (type: document), zen_benchmark-2028q2.pdf (type: pdf)
